newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: S. Australia says AN bidders mixed on Darwin link.
newsitem.headline: S. Australia says AN bidders mixed on Darwin link.

text.p: Companies considering bidding for national rail operator Australian National (AN) had shown mixed interest in plans for an Alice Springs to Darwin rail link, the South Australian government said on Tuesday.
State Premier John Olsen told reporters his government had argued that potential AN investors ought to keep the Alice-Darwin link in mind when considering their bids.
"Some have shown very keen interest, others a lukewarm interest in the Adelaide to Darwin rail link," he said.
"Suffice to say there is sufficient that are showing a keen interest that would give us encouragement," he said.
The Federal government this week passed legislation to sell AN, which operates three interstate passenger services and freight services and workshops in South Australia and Tasmania.
It has said it has drawn up a shortlist of about 12 companies interested in the rail operator or some of its assets, with analysts expecting the sell-off to raise up to about A$600 million.

Olsen said he believed final bids for AN would close on July 25, and he hoped to have some indication around that time from Canberra also on whether the Alice-Darwin link would qualify for support from a special Federation Fund for major infrastructure.
